verdicts.reason: Re-disassembly of 0x021652E8-0x0216536C matches the claim's core chain exactly, and the three debug-tag strings decode byte-for-byte as claimed: 0x021713D8='JPowerData_Create', 0x021713EC='JPowerData.cpp', 0x021713FC='bin/jpower.bin' (confirmed via `disasm` on the literal pool, not just the tracer's transcription); xrefs-to 0x021713FC shows exactly 1 reference ROM-wide, and `callers 0x021652E8` shows all 4 call-site records confined to ov5. Two minor imprecisions found but neither changes the finding: (1) the evidence_disasm silently omits 4 real instructions (0x02165300-0x0216530C, a bl-0x20517fc zero-init of the wrapper) between the alloc and file-open without any ellipsis; (2) the vtable-call description '[[r4]+4]->+0x2c' elides an extra indirection -- the actual chain is obj=[r4+0x1c]; wrapper[0]=obj; result=(*[obj])[0x2c](*[obj+4]) -- i.e. it queries a sub-object at r4+0x1c, not r4 itself.

Independent disasm of 0x02165398-0x021653CC is byte-identical to the quoted evidence: mov r2,#0x130; mul r2,r1,r2; ldr r0,[r0,#4]; ldr r0,[r0,r2] confirms entry=base+index*304, and 0x021653AC's mla chain confirms the extra r2*0x3c + r3*0x14 sub-strides. `callers`/`xrefs-to` independently reproduce the exact call-site counts (3 for 0x02165398, 9 for 0x021653AC, all ov5), and the cited example site 0x021626E8-0x021626F0 plus the constructor write at 0x021624C4 (str r4,[r8,#0x104]) both check out verbatim. Bonus corroboration the claim missed: grep of the toolkit source confirms CollisionEntry.EntrySize=20 (0x14) as claimed, but also that BattleCharacterEntry.EntrySize=60 (0x3c) exactly matches the 'unresolved' middle stride -- strengthening rather than undermining the claim.

Full disasm of function 0x020790F0 shows the loop-invariant 'mov fp,#5' at 0x02079568 (just before the loop body), confirming both divisions at 0x020795D4 (r1=fp=5) and 0x020795EC (r1=#5 literal) are genuinely /5 of the same dividend 'sl', which is a plain loop counter incremented 0..19 (cmp sl,#0x14) -- not any character/jpower field. Quotient(r0)*3<<16 and remainder(r1)*3<<16 land in adjacent stack slots, consistent with row/column grid math. No reference to char+0x56c/0x1a8/0x1b4 found in this function.

Re-ran xrefs-to 0x0200D12C (confirmed 324 branch call sites) and pool-values for both magic-multiply ranges myself: 3 hits for 0x66666667 and 1 for 0xCCCCCCCD, all in arm9; disasm of all 4 contexts shows calendar/date math (0x0205x) and a decimal-digit-extraction (itoa-style, /10 not /5) routine at 0x02052A38 -- none touch damage structures, matching round1's claim. I went further than the original sweep and checked its self-flagged Thumb-mode gap: of the 324 sites, ~15 are inside mode=thumb functions (in ov1/ov8/ov10/ov12/arm9, none in ov6); I disassembled the aligned Thumb context at each and found divisors of 2, 3, 4, 10, or 20 -- never literal 5. This closes the claim's own open question and finds no counterexample, reinforcing rather than refuting the ROM-wide conclusion, though the claim's phrase 'exhaustive check' was not literally exhaustive as originally executed (ARM-only lookback).

Disasm of 0x02156A38-0x02156A94, 0x021570EC-0x021570F4, and 0x02158B94-0x02158BAC reproduces the quoted evidence exactly. Immediately following the quoted window, the code negates both deltas (rsb r4,r0,#0 / rsb r5,r2,#0) and applies them via two calls to 0x20783cc/0x20781e4 targeting char+0x1b4 -- strong corroboration of the 'HP-like delta' interpretation the claim proposed but did not fully show. I also independently re-ran the exhaustive search-imm 0xe8 scan (134 hits, not 135 -- trivial count discrepancy) and inspected the only two arm9 str-to-+0xe8 sites myself: 0x02046914 is an unrelated global bitflag OR-in, and 0x0207C684 stores the result of helper 0x2026f94 into an unrelated object (the same helper is also called at 0x02156A90 for a different field, explaining the coincidental offset match) -- neither is the missing writer, confirming rather than refuting the claim's negative finding. The 'invoked when an attack/move starts' framing remains an inference (both 0x02156A38 and 0x021570EC show 0 direct callers, consistent with vtable dispatch), matching the tracer's own appropriately hedged PLAUSIBLE confidence rather than overclaiming.
